reason: Terminated by statute on June 14, 1935. The sole operative command approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Automatic Sprinkler Industry under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act ('do order that the said code of fair competition be and it is hereby approved'). Actor: Congress, S.J. Res. 113, section 2, approved June 14, 1935. Legal basis for the first end. An approval of a code under section 3 of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act had legal effect only through section 3: under 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry and a violation in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce was an unfair method of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and district attorneys were directed to sue, and under 3(f) each violation was a misdemeanor (the section 3 excerpt held in this packet). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935 (49 Stat. 375), repealed 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes' and states no effective date other than its approval. That repeal removed the power the approval rested on and every provision through which the approved code was enforced, which is the reason (not a default date) that it ends the prospective operative effect of this command on June 14, 1935. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495 (decided May 27, 1935), held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional ('we hold the code provisions here in question to be invalid'); the held excerpts record that as a validity characterization (an approval under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing, and May 27, 1935 is when that was declared), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no other approving order and a later doctrine treats a measure's earlier existence as an operative fact. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced the two-year expiry in section 2(c) with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935.

Exhausted by performance on October 11, 1933, the date the order is signed ('The White House, October 11, 1933'). The order's sole operative command, 'that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants, be and it is hereby denied', is a one-time determination: once made it commands nothing further. Under the shared analysis of denials of exemption, the applicants' continuing obligation after the denial is the code's own operation, which the approving order governs and which ended with the repeal; it is not a surviving command of the denial. Actor: EO 6331-A itself. Later event: section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating the power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, which ended the code obligations the denial left in place; it does not end this order, which was spent in 1933.
